note: What the manufacturer's own documentation says this silicon is. Every figure here was read out of the document named below rather than taken from an implementation of it, and each one carries the sentence or table row it came from so a later reader can check the reading rather than trusting it. This file is the authority on what the part IS. corpus.json is the authority on what the part DOES where the document is silent. When an implementation disagrees with this file, the implementation is wrong, no matter how widely used it is.

order: hardware.json, for anything the manufacturer states: widths, stack depth, cycles per instruction, memory sizes
corpus.json, for instruction-level behaviour the document does not specify: exact flag rules, undefined encodings, the result of every field combination
neither overrides the other, because they answer different questions
authority.why: corpus.json was recorded from an emulator, named in pinned.json. An emulator is a good source for behaviour nobody documented and a poor one for facts the manufacturer printed. Where the two disagree the document wins, and the recording is retaken.

dataSheet.title: uPD77C25/uPD77P25 Digital Signal Processor Data Sheet
dataSheet.note: Covers the uPD77C25 mask-ROM part and the uPD77P25 UVEPROM part, described in the document as functionally identical. This is the part Nintendo shipped as the DSP-1, DSP-2, DSP-3 and DSP-4.
dataSheet.pageNumbering: The printed number is one less than the position in the file: printed page 1 is the second page.
dataSheet.readVia: upd77c25.pdf, 36 pages, read twice. Vision read every page rendered at 300 dots per inch, and pdftotext read the layer the scan already carried. Neither is sufficient alone: the embedded layer prints lhe for the and OP for DP, while the image read misses a faint line outright, which is how the data RAM sentence came to be absent from one reading and present in the other. Every page below is one both readings agree on, or one confirmed by reading the page itself.
dataSheet.pinnedIn: the References section of README.md, and locally by digest as docs/manufacturer/upd77c25.pdf

dataBook.title: Digital Signal Processor (DSP) and Speech Processor Products Data Book
dataBook.pageNumbering: Printed numbers are per section, as 2-33. The uPD77C25 section runs from file page 76 to file page 99, and printed page 2-33 is file page 82.
dataBook.readVia: nec-dsp-data-book-1989.pdf, read twice as the other document is. The flag matrix was read from the page image at 900 dots per inch, cropped to the table, because the text layer loses the column alignment and renders the affected symbol as a digit.
dataBook.whyItMatters: The data sheet this project was built on is Advance Product Information and states no flag rules. This is the full data book for the same part, and its Table 6 gives, for every one of the sixteen ALU operations, which flags are affected, which are reset, which are held and which the manufacturer declines to define. That is the manufacturer speaking about behaviour the project had taken from a recording.

sectionPages.why: This book covers a dozen parts and several are close relatives that print the same table under the same name with the same column headings. The uPD77810 in this very book has a flag table with the identical six bits under identical names. A quote taken from it would read as perfectly sourced and would be about a different part, so every fact citing this document names the file page it came from and that page has to fall inside these.
sectionPages.howItWasFound: The running header was read off every file page from 76 onward until it changed: 76 through 99 read uPD77C25/77P25 and 100 begins the uPD77220.

clocksPerInstruction.quote: Since the 77C25 executes an instruction in one external clock cycle (versus two cycles of the same 8.192 MHz clock for 77C20A), the 77C25 may be substituted for a 77C20A (or 7720A or 77P20) in a circuit without modification of that circuit.

everyInstructionSameLength.quote: All instructions execute in one instruction cycle

instructionCycleNanoseconds.quote: Fast instruction execution: 122 ns with 8.192 MHz clock.

maximumClockHz.quote: The external clock frequency (8.3 MHz maximum) remains the same as for 7720/77C20 while the internal instruction execution speed is doubled.

programCounterBits.quote: The 2048 x 24-bit words of instruction ROM are addressed by the 11-bit program counter that can be modified by an external reset, interrupt, call, jump, or return instruction.

dataRomWords.quote: The data ROM is organized in 1024 x 16-bit words that are addressed through a 10-bit ROM pointer (RP register).

romPointerBits.quote: addressed through a 10-bit ROM pointer (RP register)

dataRamWords.quote: The data RAM is 256 x 16-bit words and is addressed through an 8-bit data pointer (DP register).

dataPointerBits.quote: The data RAM is 256 x 16-bit words and is addressed through an 8-bit data pointer (DP register).
dataPointerBits.note: The same sentence the data RAM size comes from, quoted whole rather than cut down to the clause about the pointer, so a reader finds it on the page as it is printed.

stackLevels.quote: The SPI+ contains a four-level program stack for efficient program usage and interrupt handling.
stackLevels.corroboration: The block diagram on page 7 draws the stack as four slots, labelled 0, 1, 2 and 3.
stackLevels.notStated: What happens on a fifth consecutive call is not stated in this document. A two-bit pointer wrapping to slot zero is the consequence of the width the document gives, and the model takes that, but it is an inference from the width rather than a figure the document prints.

flagsPerAccumulator.quote: In addition to zero result, sign, carry, and overflow flags, the SPI+ incorporates auxiliary overflow and sign flags (SA1, SB1, OVA1, OVB1). These flags enable the detection of an overflow condition and maintain the correct sign after as many as three successive additions or subtractions.

multiplier.quote: Thirty-one-bit results are developed by a 16 x 16-bit two's complement multiplier in 122 ns. The result is automatically latched to two 16-bit registers, M and N, at the end of each instruction cycle. The sign bit and 15 higher bits are in M and the 16 lower bits are in N; the LSB in N is zero. A new product is available for use after every instruction cycle

aluOperations.quote: The ALU is a 16-bit two's complement unit capable of executing 16 distinct operations on data routed via the P and Q ALU inputs.

interruptVector.quote: A low-to-high transition on this pin executes a call instruction to location 100H, if interrupts were previously enabled.

resetSetsProgramCounterTo.quote: This input initializes the SPI+ internal logic and sets the PC to 0.

statusDataRegisterSelect.quote: A0 [Status Data Register Select] This input selects data register for read/write (low) or status register for read (high).

serialNanosecondsPerBit.note: Two instruction cycles per serial bit at 8.192 MHz. Nothing in a cartridge uses the serial port.

instructionElementOrder.quote: To control the execution of instructions, the external 8 MHz clock is divided into phases for internal execution. The various elements of the 24-bit instruction word are executed in a set order. Multiplication automatically begins first. Also, data moves from source to destination before other elements of the instruction. Data being moved on the internal data bus (IDB) is available for use in ALU operations (if P-select of the instruction specifies IDB).
instructionElementOrder.andAlso: Pointer modifications occur at the end of the instruction cycle after their values have been used for data moves. The result of multiplication is available at the end of the instruction cycle for possible use in the next instruction. If a return is specified as part of an OP instruction, it is executed last.

arithmeticSupersededByItsOwnDestination.quote: However, if the accumulator specified in the ASL field is also specified as the destination of the data move, the ALU operation becomes a NOP, as the data move supersedes the ALU operation.
arithmeticSupersededByItsOwnDestination.consequence: A NOP is the one operation that leaves the flags alone: "These flags ... are updated at the end of each arithmetic instruction (except NOP)", and the ALU table gives NOP no flag effects at all. So the arithmetic must not run, rather than run and be overwritten. A model that overwrites holds the right accumulator and the wrong flags, and the next conditional branch reads those flags.
arithmeticSupersededByItsOwnDestination.foundBy: Reading this page. Both implementations here ran the arithmetic and let the move overwrite it, and so does the emulator the corpus was recorded from: 581 of the 22,240 recorded cases changed when it was fixed.

statusRegisterBits.quote: Figure 3. Status Register (SR): bit 15 RQM, 14 USF1, 13 USF0, 12 DRS, 11 DMA, 10 DRC, 9 SOC, 8 SIC, 7 EI, bits 6 to 2 zero, 1 P1, 0 P0
statusRegisterBits.note: Checked against both implementations here and they already matched, bit for bit.

requestBitSemantics.quote: RQM (Request for Master): A read or write form DR to IDB sets RQM = 1, An external read (write) resets RQM = 0.
requestBitSemantics.note: The part raises it when its own program touches the data register; the console clears it by reading or writing. Checked against the implementation here and it already matched.

transferHalfSemantics.quote: DRS (DR Status): For 16-bit DR transfers (DRC = 0), DRS = 1 after first 8 bits have been transferred. DRS = 0 after all 16 bits have been transferred.

statusReadWidth.quote: Eight MSBs of SR are output to D0-D7
statusReadWidth.note: The read width already matched. A write to the status port does nothing here, which is the least surprising reading of illegal.

parallelInterfaceIsEightBit.note: So a sixteen-bit data register is moved a byte at a time, which is what DRS tracks.

aluFlagMatrix.quote: Notes: May be affected, depending on the results; Previous status can be held; Reset; Indefinite

legend.affected: May be affected, depending on the results

aluFlagMatrix.whatItSettles: Which flags each ALU operation touches, from the manufacturer rather than from the recording. It confirms the split this model already made: only the one-bit shifts take the carry from the bit shifted out, while the two-bit and four-bit shifts, the exchange, the complement and the three logic operations reset it.
aluFlagMatrix.whatItLeavesOpen: The auxiliary sign flag is declared indefinite for the logic operations, the complement, the exchange and every shift. This model gives it a definite value there, following the recording, because a model has to answer something. That is a choice this project makes and not a figure the manufacturer gives.

clockCycleNanoseconds.note: The symbol every other timing figure in the document is given in. One clock cycle is one instruction on this part, so a figure quoted in tCYC is a figure in instructions.

resetPulseCycles.quote: RST Pulse Width tRST 4 tCYC ns
resetPulseCycles.note: The minimum the host must hold the reset line, not a count of what the part does internally, which the document does not give. This model spends it, because a board that pulls the line has spent it.

interruptPulseCycles.quote: INT Pulse Width tINT 3 tCYC ns; INT Recovery Time tRINT 2 tCYC ns
interruptPulseCycles.note: What the host must hold the interrupt line for, and how long it must wait before raising it again. Recorded because it is the manufacturer speaking about a pin this package does not yet drive.

predecessorForContrast.why: Recorded because a reader who finds a 250 ns instruction cycle quoted for this family has found the earlier part. Taking that figure for this one would halve the rate at which it runs.
predecessorForContrast.section: the comparison table on printed page 3, which sets the two parts side by side

unverified.note: No manufacturer document for this part was located. Everything asserted about it below therefore rests on secondary sources, and secondary sources for this family are emulators, which is the weakest kind of evidence this project accepts for a fact the manufacturer would have printed. It is recorded as unverified rather than quietly adopted.

whatThisProjectUses.why: The three memory sizes are corroborated by the images themselves: an ST010 firmware file is exactly 16384 program words of three bytes plus 2048 table words of two bytes, so a wrong size would not load. The stack depth has no such corroboration. Eight is used because it is what the secondary sources say and because it is the smallest value consistent with them; the measurement in the sibling project shows no microcode in the family reaching past slot three, so the exposure of being wrong here is small but it is not zero.

unverified.howToSettleIt: A NEC data book covering the uPD96050, or a decapped part. Until one is read, this entry stays marked unverified and the README says so.
